employees.summary: The most active person on the roster and the one carrying the most risk. Mayson appears in all 14 active client chats, routes escalations nobody else routes, and is repeatedly described by the client analysts as the only reason some accounts get answered at all. But he closed zero commitments this week against 32 overdue, and two patterns turned harmful. First, he ran an uncoordinated Facebook-access campaign: the identical message 'do you have a facebook account available to use?' went to at least six clients on 2026-09-16 alone, including one two days after she warned she might leave, one 21 days post-surgery, and one who had already given ALTR that access in June. Second, and more seriously, he solicited live credentials and 2FA codes directly in group chats that contain outsourced vendor accounts. In Sarah Lloyd's chat he asked for a Snapchat 2FA code 3 hours 48 minutes after Mica posted a security advisory into that same thread telling the client never to send codes to anyone, including ALTR. He is not the cause of the credential policy gap, but he is its most frequent trigger, and that needs to stop this week.
